evidence: Quint. 3.2: in medicīnā … alia salūbria, alia īnsalūbria
terms.comment: A description, from Pliny’s and Quintilian’s īnsalūbris, “unwholesome”. No reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for junk food; for food eaten in a hurry or bought to take away, see “fast food”.

phrases.latin: Cibī īnsalūbrēs sunt; nē nimium ēderīs.
phrases.english: That’s junk food; don’t eat too much of it.

phrases.latin: Hominēs enim sīcut in medicīnā, cum vidērent alia salūbria, alia īnsalūbria, ex observātiōne eōrum effēcērunt artem
phrases.english: For just as in medicine, when people saw that some things were wholesome and others unwholesome, they made an art out of observing them
